slides.heading: Split Binary Tree
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Medium · Binary Trees
slides.narration: Let's solve Split Binary Tree, a medium binary trees problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Can removing one edge split the tree into two parts with equal sums?
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Can removing one edge split the tree into two parts with equal sums? Return that half-sum, else 0.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: We need a subtree whose sum is exactly half the total.
slides.narration: We need a subtree whose sum is exactly half the total.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Brute force: try cutting each edge, re-sum both parts → O(n²)
Two passes: total, then post-order subtree sums → O(n)
Need a subtree (not the whole tree) = total / 2
slides.narration: Cutting each edge and re-summing both parts is quadratic. Instead compute the total once, then a post-order pass gives every subtree sum; if any non-root subtree equals half the total, we can split.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 4. Return true if any subtree equals half
slides.narration: Step by step. First, compute the total sum. Second, if odd, it can't split. Third, post-order subtree sums. Fourth, return true if any subtree equals half.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Total sum = 12 → need a subtree summing to 6
slides.narration: The whole tree sums to 12, which is even, so we need some subtree summing to exactly 6.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Subtree at 3 sums to 6 → cut its edge
slides.narration: The subtree rooted at 3 sums to 6. Cutting the edge above it splits the tree into two halves of 6 each.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: We sum the whole tree; if the total is odd we return zero. Then check computes each subtree sum in post-order and sets a flag when a non-root subtree equals half.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n. Space is O of h.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Negative values make greedy pruning unsafe
slides.narration: An odd total can't split. Exclude the root, since cutting nothing isn't a split. With negative values, you can't prune early.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
bullets: Follow-up: maximise product of the two parts
slides.narration: This version returns the half sum, or zero. A popular follow-up maximises the product of the two parts.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: We need a subtree whose sum is exactly half the total.
slides.narration: To recap Split Binary Tree: We need a subtree whose sum is exactly half the total. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
